<http://link.myjewishpage.com/scripts/image_cdo/a/e/i/IAMtYyEMhwY_:DDCB8AC0FCC3A1F104AA7513C6ADB09085F6

Dear Friends, 
Chanukah begins this Sunday evening. The first candle is lit this Sunday night December 6th at nightfall or after dark. We 
continue lighting the candles each night for eight nights. The last night we light the candles is Sunday night December 
13th . On Friday December 11, one must light the candles only before sunset and not afterwards. On Saturday 
December 12th, one must only light the candles at least one hour after sunset and not before. 
Please make the extra effort and the light the Chanukah candles this year. 
You do not have to have an actual Menorah to fulfill this Mitzvah(requirement). You can use any candle or any type of 
oil you have in the house and still fulfill the Mitzvah of lighting Chanukah lights . If you do not have a Menorah or 
Chanukah candles and cannot buy a menorah or Chanukah candles locally, please email me and we will help you locate a 
menorah and candles in your area or send you some. 
Each and every Jew should light his or her own Menorah with real candles or oil. Children are encouraged to light as 
well. 
The Blessings 
Before lighting the Chanukah candles, we thank G-d for giving us this special mitzvah, and for the incredible Chanukah 
miracles: 
Ba-ruch A-tah Ado-nai E-lo-he-nu Me-lech ha-olam a-sher ki-de-sha-nu be-mitz-vo-tav ve-tzi-va-nu le-had-lik ner 
Chanukah. 
Ba-ruch A-tah Ado-nai E-lo-hei-nu Me-lech ha-olam she-a-sa ni-sim la-avo-te-nu ba-ya-mim ha-hem bi-z'man ha-zeh. 
(Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe, who has sanctified us with His commandments, and commanded 
us to kindle the Chanukah light. 
Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe, who performed miracles for our forefathers in those days, at this 
time.] 
The first time you light the menorah each year , one should add the following blessing: 
EFTA_R1_00006972 
EFTA01733235
--- PAGE 2 ---
Baruch A-tah Ado-nal E-to-he•nu Me•lech ha-olam she-heche-ya-nu ve•ki-yi-ma-nu ve-higi-a-nu liz-man ha-zeh. 
[Blessed are You, lord our God, King of the universe, who has granted us life, sustained us, and enabled us to reach this 
occasion.] 
For everything you want to know about the holiday of Chanukah including recipes for Potato Latkes, visit 
www.chanukah.org
